cards.text: Friend, Joshua 12 is a roll call of the kings the Israelites struck down and whose lands they took. I spent years in a junk drawer counting dust, so believe me, I was BORN for a list. We start east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley all the way up to Mount Hermon.

Two kings held that side. Sihon king of the Amorites lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, ruled over Mount Hermon and all of Bashan. That's a big name with a BIG title, and the most impressive thing on my handle is the word Dorin.

cards.question: Joshua was the one leading Israel when Sihon and Og were struck down.
Moses gave the land of Sihon and Og as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of ___.

cards.text: Now cross the river, friend, because the west side is Joshua's turn. He and the Israelites conquered kings from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir.

cards.question: Moses gave the land east of the Jordan to the tribes. What does Joshua do with the land he conquered in the west?

answers.text: He gives it to the tribes as an inheritance
He keeps it under his own rule for now
He leaves it empty until the next battle

cards.question: The land in the west that Joshua handed out had been the lands of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

cards.text: Then comes the roll call, and every king gets the same little tag: the king of Jericho, one, the king of Ai, one, then Jerusalem, Hebron, Lachish, Hazor, one, one, ONE, all the way down to the king of Tirzah. Add it up and it's thirty-one kings in all, and friend, I counted dust for YEARS and never once got a total that good.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Two kings held that side.', the sentence naming Sihon and Og, and the handle joke. Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions Moses or says who led Israel east of the Jordan. Card 2 names only Sihon and Og, so the baker can only guess whether Joshua led. Cards 3 and 4 are both pure discovery questions, and card 7 is a list-recall question, so most of the stop's choice cards are not informed guesses.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the tribe list in 12:6 (Manasseh versus Ephraim or Benjamin). No card gives any setup for it, so the baker is guessing wording they haven't seen, not reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to confirm the list of six peoples in 12:8. That list is land and name detail inside a long stretch, so it should not get a choice card.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Joshua 12 is entirely land boundaries and a list of kings, so the whole passage counts as a long stretch. The docs conflict here. A long stretch gets one story card, never gets a choice card, and never gets a stop of its own. But every stop needs at least as many choice cards as story cards. The walkthrough worked around this by asking choice cards on list details (cards 3, 4 and 7).
findings.question: When a whole passage is a long stretch, like Joshua 12, how should Prep be built? Should the east/west split and who gave the land count as moments that can get choice cards? Should the long-stretch rule be relaxed? Or should the choice-to-story ratio be waived for passages like this?
